detailed_description: Live-action 1970s Shaw Brothers historical studio cinema, ancient Troy, saturated 35mm film colors, theatrical hard light, practical timber and stone sets. One enormous hollow wooden Trojan horse, visibly made from timber planks with the same golden bronze bands, mounted on the same four-wheeled timber platform. Its four rigid wooden legs never walk, its head never moves, and its wheels rotate only while pulled. One rectangular hinged hatch on its camera-facing belly and one wooden ladder. The Greek leader is the bearded short-dark-haired man in engraved bronze armor and a red cloak, with one sword sheathed at his right hip and no shield. His companion is the clean-shaven curly-dark-haired man in engraved bronze armor and a blue cloak, with one sword sheathed at his right hip and one round bronze shield strapped to his back. They use free hands to climb. Keep faces, hair, armor, cloak colors, equipment ownership and horse construction consistent. [Shot 1] Night. Continue the same camera movement and unfolding action without a cut. The red-cloaked bearded Greek leader climbs down the ladder from the open belly hatch, steps from the timber platform onto the square, looks around and signals quietly with his empty left hand. The clean-shaven curly-haired blue-cloaked companion emerges from that SAME hatch and climbs down the SAME ladder behind him, shield strapped to his back and sword sheathed. Exactly these two Greek soldiers emerge in sequence, no fight. The wooden horse and platform remain motionless. overall_soundscape: Quiet night wind, ladder creaks, sandals land on stone, soft armor rustle and torches. No dialogue or music. non_diegetic_music: None.
